diagnostic_tracker.title: Will It? Maybe! — Day 1 Diagnostic Checklist
diagnostic_tracker.when_used: During Lesson 1, while children are at the likelihood-naming stations.
diagnostic_tracker.usage_notes: Walk between pairs. Tick where you see clear evidence. The 'Names impossible' and 'Names certain' columns are the easier signals; 'Names possible' is harder because it requires recognizing uncertainty.

summative_rubric.title: Will It? Maybe! — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: Used during and after Lesson 5 (Likelihood Lab Capstone) to score each child against both expectations on a 4-level scale. Aligned with Ontario Grade 1 Communication of Learning conventions.

rows.expectation_text: use mathematical language, including the terms “impossible”, “possible”, and “certain”, to describe the likelihood of events happening, and use that likelihood to make predictions and informed decisions

levels.descriptor: Cannot consistently distinguish the 3 likelihood terms. Defaults to 'possible' or 'maybe' for everything.
Names IMPOSSIBLE and CERTAIN with prompts. Uses POSSIBLE for genuinely uncertain events.
Independently uses all 3 likelihood terms appropriately. Makes predictions using likelihood reasoning.
Justifies likelihood assignments with real-world reasoning. Predicts the MORE LIKELY outcome and explains why.

rows.expectation_text: make and test predictions about the likelihood that the categories in a data set from one population will have the same frequencies in data collected from a different population of the same size

levels.descriptor: Predicts but does not yet TEST in another group. Insists original prediction is right despite different test results.
Tests in a second group with adult prompts. Sometimes accepts that results differ.
Independently makes a prediction, tests it in a different group, and accepts that results may differ across groups.
Predicts for two groups separately and reasons about WHY results may differ ('different families, different favourites').

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Score during the Lesson 5 capstone (visible from the Lab Template) and confirm during the share. Level 3 is the grade-level expectation. Communicate scores to families using Communication of Learning narrative.
summative_rubric.layout_description: One letter page, landscape orientation, with a 2-row × 4-level grid table plus a left-most column for expectation code and text. Title at top; usage notes below.

summative_task_script.title: Likelihood Lab Capstone — Summative Administration Guide
summative_task_script.purpose: Ties the Lesson 5 Lab Template, the 4-step predict-test-record cycle, and the rubric together. Tells the teacher exactly what evidence to look for at each station.
administration_steps: Before the lesson: photocopy one Lab Template per child plus 5 extras. Print rubric or maintain class-wide rubric on a clipboard. Have Junior Likelihood Detective certificates ready.
Station 1 (COIN, 5 min): predict + test 5 flips. Evidence for D2.1 (likelihood word: possible).
Station 2 (DICE, 5 min): predict + test 5 rolls. Evidence for D2.1.
Station 3 (MARBLES, 5 min): predict + test 5 pulls (4 red + 1 blue). Evidence for D2.1 (more likely = red) + D2.2 (test in different colour ratio).
Station 4 (WEATHER, 5 min): predict tomorrow's weather. Evidence for D2.1.
Station 5 (SORT, 5 min): sort 6 events. Evidence for D2.1 categorization.
After: review the Lab Template with each child. For below-Level-3, note evidence and use for Communication of Learning.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Use the Lab Template as primary evidence. Level 3 = grade-level. L4 children ready for Grade 2 likelihood. L1 children need targeted small-group work in the next math block.

evidence_per_expectation.D2.1: Look at Stations 1-2-3-4 (predictions). Did the child predict using likelihood reasoning (e.g., 'more likely red because more red marbles')? Combined with Station 5 (sort). A child who predicts before testing AND sorts correctly is at Level 3.
evidence_per_expectation.D2.2: Look at Station 3 (marbles). Did the child predict and accept actual test results, even if they differed from prediction? A child who reports honestly (regardless of right/wrong) is at Level 3.
